archetype.name: Game Manager (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old, 14-year journeyman who wins by staying on schedule, getting the ball out before pressure lands and hitting the middle of the field off play-action, but who lacks the arm talent or accuracy to carry an offense from behind.

report.headline: One tidy spot start, one ugly relief outing, and now third on the depth chart
report.take:
Keenum is what he has been for most of a long career: a competent caretaker who can run a functioning offense when the script holds and struggles once it doesn't. His career has one real peak, the 2017 Vikings season with 22 TDs and a +3.6 CPOE, set among years of below-average efficiency and mostly negative CPOE. At 38.8 he came into 2026 as insurance behind Caleb Williams. He started Week 3, then played a third of the snaps in the Week 5 loss at Green Bay, a game Tyson Bagent started. As of Nov. 17 he is the QB3, and Williams has started every game since Week 6.

The two games point in opposite directions, and the split is mostly about game state. Against Philadelphia, a defense now ranked 27th, he went 24 of 34 for 247 yards and 2 TDs. He added +6.6 EPA, worked from a 2.41-second time to throw and threw only 8.8% bad balls. At Green Bay, the 7th-ranked defense, he went 11 of 19 for 108 with an interception, a lost fumble, two sacks and a 31.6% bad-throw rate. Across the season he was +0.305 EPA per play within one score and -0.448 when trailing by 9 or more. Under center he was +0.655 on 14 plays, in the shotgun -0.291 on 41. That is the Ben Johnson offense working as designed in the first set of numbers, and a backup QB asked to throw his team back into a game in the second.

The headline rates flatter him a little. His 3.6% sack rate (2nd of 54) and 12.7% pressured rate (3rd of 42) come more from a quick, short-area plan than from pocket escapability. When pressure did get home, 28.6% of it turned into sacks, 22nd of 42. His bad-throw rate of 17% ranks 35th of 42, and his tracking CPOE is -3.27. His intermediate numbers (+0.613 EPA on 11 attempts) are the best thing on the sheet, but 11 throws is a hint, not a skill read. His deep game was four attempts and one completion. The dossier also shows his dropbacks adding up to -3.6 EPA once sacks and scrambles are counted, against +1.6 on passes alone.

Going forward this is a depth-chart story, not a performance one. As QB3 he needs two injuries, or a blowout deep enough to empty the bench past Bagent, to see the field. If he does play, expect the Week 3 version against weak defenses with a lead and the Week 5 version against good ones from behind.

strengths.title: Gets the ball out before pressure
strengths.body: He was rarely pressured and rarely sacked, mainly because the plan had him throwing short and on time. His intended air yards sat at 7.44, 0.76 short of the sticks. This is a career-long trait: he posted solid pressure-to-sack ranks in 2018 and 2019. It is a real, repeatable way he protects an offense, though it also caps the upside.

strengths.title: On-script, under-center efficiency
strengths.body: When the game is close and the offense can use play-action and under-center looks, he executes. He completed 92.9% of his under-center throws for +0.655 EPA, and his work in one-score games was clearly above average. The samples are small, but the pattern matches what veteran game managers do in a well-designed system.

strengths.title: Spot start was genuinely good
strengths.body: His one full start produced +0.195 EPA per dropback and no sacks or interceptions. That is well above the league-average passEpaPerDropback of -0.021 and a real asset for a backup. It came against a defense now ranked 27th, so read it as a floor-raiser against weak opponents rather than proof of more.

concerns.title: Accuracy is below average
concerns.body: Stripped of scheme help, his ball placement is a weakness. A 17% bad-throw rate ranks 35th of 42, his tracking CPOE is negative, and the Green Bay outing saw nearly a third of his throws charted as bad. His career CPOE has been negative in every season but 2017, so this is who he is rather than a slump.

concerns.title: Can't play from behind
concerns.body: Once the offense moved to shotgun and obvious passing downs, his efficiency fell apart: -0.291 EPA per shotgun play and -0.448 when trailing by 9 or more, with both sacks and his interception coming in that game state. He also converted only 36.4% of third downs at an average of 8.4 yards to go. He lacks the arm or mobility to create when the structure breaks.

concerns.title: Buried at QB3
concerns.body: The biggest factor is role. He is listed third on the depth chart, and Williams has started every game since Week 6. His meaningful snaps this year came in two early-season games. Barring injuries above him, his weekly output projects close to zero.

trend.note: He followed an efficient Week 3 start with a rough partial game at Green Bay. He has not appeared in the log since and has slid from starter to QB3.

nextGame.headline: Big favorite at home, but only blowout snaps would reach him
nextGame.body:
New Orleans is an inviting defense on paper. It ranks 23rd in EPA allowed, 20th against the pass and 31st on deep throws, and it gives WR1s 3.3 PPR points over their norm. The one feature that suits Keenum is that Chicago is an 11.5-point favorite with a -650 moneyline. A comfortable lead is exactly the state where a backup gets mop-up work. But he would need the game out of reach and the staff willing to go past Bagent, and his own leading-by-9 sample (5 plays) was poor. Wind of 16 mph with 26 mph gusts is in an early forecast and could trim passing if it holds.

Availability mostly points toward a lopsided game. The Saints' offensive line is depleted: right tackle Taliese Fuaga and center Erik McCoy are out, and Asim Richards is sidelined for weeks. That should help Chicago's 3rd-ranked pass rush build a lead. On the Bears' side, left tackle Braxton Jones is done for the year. Luther Burden III, the receiver Keenum targeted most, is questionable with a concussion but practiced Monday. Keenum himself carries an Out designation on the site with no injury listed, so treat any snaps as unlikely.

keyMatchups.title: Spread sets up garbage time
keyMatchups.body: An 11.5-point spread is the only realistic path to the field for a QB3. Even in a blowout, Bagent sits ahead of him. Keenum's handful of snaps with a big lead went badly, though the five-play sample means little.

keyMatchups.title: Saints pass rush vs quick game
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans gets home, with the 5th-best sack rate. Keenum's short, on-time style kept his sack rate tiny, but when he held the ball at Green Bay he took two sacks and lost a fumble.

keyMatchups.title: Wind in the early forecast
keyMatchups.body: Sustained wind of 16 mph with 26 mph gusts would tilt Chicago further toward the run with a lead. That shrinks passing volume for whichever quarterback is in. The forecast is more than three days out, so hold it loosely.

nextGame.watch: Whether Chicago builds a big enough lead that it rests Williams, and whether Bagent or Keenum takes those snaps.

restOfSeason.body:
As QB3 his expected weekly output is essentially nil, which is why the projections sit near zero. Only an injury to Williams with Bagent also unavailable, or a deep blowout, changes that. If he were pressed into a start, the reasonable expectation is something between his two games. Against a soft defense with a lead he can run Johnson's under-center, play-action offense efficiently and keep the sack count down, as he did against Philadelphia. Against a good defense or from behind, the bad-throw rate and lack of a deep game surface, as they did at Green Bay.

What is sustainable is the low sack rate and the short, on-schedule profile, which he has shown for years. What would regress is the intermediate efficiency, which rests on 11 throws, and the small-sample under-center accuracy. A 92.9% completion rate there is not a real level for a career below-average-CPOE passer.
swingFactors: Health of Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent
Blowout game scripts that empty the bench
Burden's return if Keenum is ever pressed into action

confidence.note: Only 57 dropbacks, but his QB3 role makes the outlook clear.
